item.content:encoded:
The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) is inviting applications for a Regional Integration (RI) Graduate Intern to support research, policy development, regional coordination, stakeholder engagement, and program implementation.

This opportunity is particularly relevant for recent postgraduate graduates who want to build professional experience in economic research, regional integration, international development, public policy, data analysis, and African economic transformation.

The position is based in Accra, Ghana, with remote work arrangements available, and the successful intern will work under the supervision of a Senior Policy Analyst within ACET’s Regional Integration Program.

Applications are open until Thursday, 27 August 2026.

Opportunity Overview

  • Organization: African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET)
  • Opportunity: Regional Integration Graduate Intern
  • Job Title: Graduate Intern – Regional Integration (RI)
  • Category: Internship
  • Location: Accra / Remote
  • Posted: 13 August 2026
  • Reporting to: Senior Policy Analyst
  • Application deadline: Thursday, 27 August 2026
  • Application method: Email application
  • Application email: pnc@acetforafrica.org
  • Interview format: Virtual or in person for candidates based in Ghana
  • Target applicants: Recent postgraduate graduates, particularly those with backgrounds in Economics or related Social Sciences

About the African Center for Economic Transformation

The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) is an African economic policy institute focused on supporting Africa’s long-term economic transformation.

The organization conducts research, provides policy advice, and works to encourage practical action that can help African countries develop stronger economies, reduce poverty, and improve livelihoods.

ACET describes itself as an organization focused on advancing African solutions to African challenges. Its work brings together research, policy thinking, partnerships, and practical approaches to economic transformation across the continent.

For an aspiring policy professional, researcher, development practitioner, economist, or analyst, an internship with an institution such as ACET can provide exposure to the intersection of research, public policy, economic development, regional cooperation, and government engagement.

About the Regional Integration Program

The internship is situated within ACET’s Regional Integration (RI) Program.

Regional integration is an important component of Africa’s economic development agenda. It involves strengthening economic relationships between African countries, improving cross-border trade and cooperation, supporting regional value chains, and identifying policies that can help countries participate more effectively in regional and continental markets.

The intern will therefore have the opportunity to contribute to work connected to regional value chain development, while gaining exposure to research, program coordination, stakeholder engagement, partnerships, reporting, and business development.

Role and Purpose of the Internship

The Regional Integration Program is looking for a graduate intern who can provide support across several areas of its work.

The role is designed around three broad areas:

  1. Research and analysis
  2. Program coordination and implementation
  3. Stakeholder engagement

The intern will also contribute to communications and knowledge products, business development activities, and administrative support when required.

This makes the opportunity broader than a traditional research internship. The successful candidate is expected to combine analytical ability, strong writing, organizational skills, communication skills, and the ability to work effectively with different stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

1. Research and Data Analysis

A major component of the position involves supporting ACET’s research activities.

The intern will assist project teams with:

  • Collecting relevant research data.
  • Organizing and analyzing information.
  • Interpreting data.
  • Synthesizing research findings.
  • Providing inputs into research reports.
  • Supporting evidence-based analysis.
  • Contributing to the development of research outputs.

This responsibility makes research ability particularly important for applicants.

Candidates should be comfortable working with information from different sources, identifying relevant evidence, understanding findings, and communicating analytical conclusions clearly.

2. Cross-Country Project Coordination

The intern will support coordination across projects involving different countries and stakeholders.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Supporting communication between project teams.
  • Helping coordinate activities across countries.
  • Assisting with project-related follow-up.
  • Engaging stakeholders during research validation processes.
  • Supporting dissemination of research findings.
  • Helping ensure project activities progress according to established plans.

This aspect of the role could provide valuable experience for candidates interested in project management, international development, policy coordination, consulting, and regional development.

3. Policy Briefs, Blogs and Thought Pieces

The successful candidate will also support the program’s communications and knowledge-sharing activities.

This includes working with the program Lead to develop:

  • Thought pieces.
  • Policy briefs.
  • Blogs.
  • Research narratives.
  • Key messages related to regional integration.

The objective is to make complex research and policy findings easier for policymakers and other stakeholders to understand and use.

Strong writing skills will therefore be important.

Applicants should be able to take research information, identify the most important findings, and communicate those findings in a clear and accessible way.

4. Business Development Support

The intern may also contribute to ACET’s business development activities.

This could involve conducting background research to support the preparation of technical proposals.

Candidates interested in consulting, development organizations, research institutes, policy institutions, or international organizations may find this aspect of the role particularly valuable because it provides exposure to how organizations develop proposals around technical and policy projects.

5. Administrative Support

The intern will provide additional administrative support to the Regional Integration Program when required.

This may involve helping with coordination, documentation, communication, scheduling, reporting, research organization, and other activities necessary for effective program implementation.

The role therefore requires someone who is not only academically capable but also organized, dependable, adaptable, and comfortable handling multiple responsibilities.

Educational Requirements

Applicants should have a minimum of a postgraduate degree in Economics or a related field in the Social Sciences.

Relevant academic backgrounds may include areas such as:

  • Economics
  • Development Economics
  • International Development
  • Public Policy
  • Political Science
  • International Relations
  • Development Studies
  • Public Administration
  • Other closely related Social Science disciplines

However, applicants should carefully assess whether their postgraduate qualification is sufficiently related to the role before applying.

Professional and Relevant Experience

Previous professional experience is not presented as an absolute requirement, but relevant experience will strengthen an application.

ACET specifically indicates that experience gained through:

  • Employment
  • Volunteering
  • Internships
  • Research
  • International development activities
  • Economic research
  • Related development work

can be an advantage.

The internship is intended for recent graduates who are looking to gain practical experience and transition into the world of work.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their academic background, research projects, internships, volunteer work, employment, or other experiences have prepared them to contribute to the Regional Integration Program.

Required Skills and Abilities

Excellent Research Skills

Research is central to this internship.

Applicants should be able to:

  • Find and evaluate relevant information.
  • Conduct structured research.
  • Organize evidence.
  • Analyze information.
  • Draw meaningful conclusions.
  • Contribute to research reports.

Data Analysis Skills

The position also requires candidates who can support data collection and analysis.

Applicants should demonstrate their ability to work with data and translate information into useful findings.

Where applicable, candidates should highlight relevant coursework, research projects, professional assignments, or technical tools they have used for data analysis.

Strong Writing Skills

Writing is another major requirement.

The intern may contribute to:

  • Research reports
  • Policy briefs
  • Blogs
  • Thought pieces
  • Technical proposals
  • Research summaries

Applicants should therefore ensure that their CV and cover letter demonstrate clear, professional, analytical writing.

French Language Skills

ACET states that candidates should possess a good working knowledge of French.

This is an important requirement because the position involves regional and cross-country work.

Applicants who have French-language qualifications, professional experience using French, academic exposure to French, or practical communication ability should clearly indicate this in their application.

Teamwork

The intern will work with project teams and interact with colleagues and stakeholders.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate the ability to:

  • Collaborate effectively.
  • Contribute to team projects.
  • Communicate professionally.
  • Support colleagues.
  • Work across different assignments.

Ability to Work With Limited Oversight

The organization is also looking for candidates who can work comfortably with limited supervision.

This means applicants should demonstrate:

  • Initiative
  • Self-management
  • Accountability
  • Time management
  • Problem-solving
  • The ability to complete assigned tasks independently

Personal Qualities ACET Is Looking For

Beyond academic qualifications and technical skills, ACET highlights several personal qualities.

Interpersonal Skills

The successful candidate should have outstanding interpersonal skills and be able to communicate effectively with different people.

Organizational Skills

Because the position combines research, coordination, stakeholder engagement, communications, business development, and administrative responsibilities, strong organization will be essential.

Communication Skills

The intern will interact with colleagues, partners, government officials, and stakeholders from different backgrounds and cultures.

Professional verbal and written communication will therefore be important.

Administrative Ability

Candidates should also be capable of handling administrative responsibilities efficiently and professionally.

ACET’s Core Values

Applicants should understand the values of the organization before applying.

ACET identifies five core values:

Pioneering

ACET seeks to push boundaries and operate in the spirit of a “think and do” tank.

Respect

The organization emphasizes mutual respect and believes that people grow by respecting one another.

Integrity

Transparency and accountability are central to ACET’s approach.

Collaboration

ACET believes that strong results are achieved when people work effectively together.

Excellence

The organization strives for high standards of critical thinking and seeks effective solutions to difficult challenges.

A strong cover letter should ideally show how the applicant’s own experience and working style align with these values.

Who Should Apply?

This internship is particularly suited to recent postgraduate graduates who want to build professional experience in economic research, regional integration, public policy, international development, or related fields.

Potentially relevant applicants include graduates with postgraduate qualifications in:

  • Economics
  • Development Economics
  • Development Studies
  • Political Science
  • International Relations
  • Public Policy
  • Public Administration
  • Other related Social Sciences

Applicants with relevant research, internship, volunteer, or professional experience may have an additional advantage.

The opportunity may also appeal to people seeking to build careers as:

  • Policy analysts
  • Economic researchers
  • Development professionals
  • Research analysts
  • Project coordinators
  • International development practitioners
  • Public policy professionals
  • Regional integration specialists
  • Management or development consultants

Countries and Geographic Eligibility

The vacancy does not state a nationality restriction.

The position is listed as Accra/Remote, and ACET describes itself as a Pan-African organization with a diversified African and global talent base.

Candidates should therefore focus primarily on meeting the stated educational, professional, language, research, analytical, and interpersonal requirements.

Candidates based in Ghana should note that interviews may be conducted in person, while virtual interviews may also be used.

Because the vacancy does not explicitly specify a list of eligible countries or a nationality requirement, applicants outside Ghana should confirm their ability to participate remotely and their eligibility before submitting an application.

Is This an Internship, Job, Scholarship or Fellowship?

Category: Internship

This is a graduate internship opportunity, not a scholarship, conference, award, competition, fellowship, grant, or permanent employment position.

ACET explicitly notes that the internship does not guarantee employment after the internship.

Applicants should therefore view the opportunity primarily as a professional development and experience-building opportunity.

What Can Applicants Gain From the Opportunity?

Although the vacancy does not advertise a specific financial benefit or salary package, the responsibilities indicate several potentially valuable professional development opportunities.

Research Experience

Participants can gain practical exposure to economic and policy research, including data collection, analysis, interpretation, and report development.

Policy Writing Experience

The intern can contribute to policy briefs, blogs, thought pieces, and other research communications.

Regional Development Exposure

Working within the Regional Integration Program can expose the intern to issues involving African economic integration and regional value chains.

Cross-Country Coordination

The role provides exposure to projects involving multiple countries and stakeholders.

Stakeholder Engagement

The intern may interact with partners, policymakers, government officials, and other stakeholders.

Business Development

The position also offers exposure to technical proposal development and background research for business development activities.

Professional Networking

Working within a Pan-African policy institution can provide opportunities to develop professional relationships with researchers, policy professionals, development practitioners, government stakeholders, and other experts.

How to Apply

Interested applicants are required to submit:

  1. A current CV
  2. A cover letter explaining why they are the most suitable candidate

Applications should be submitted by email to:

pnc@acetforafrica.org

Applicants should ensure that their CV and cover letter are tailored specifically to the Regional Integration Graduate Intern position.

More information about this internship, visit ACET for Africa

For more global internship programs visit the OFY Website HERE 

How to Make Your Application Stronger

Tailor Your CV

Do not submit a generic CV if you can avoid it.

Highlight experiences related to:

  • Research
  • Data analysis
  • Policy
  • Economics
  • Development
  • Regional integration
  • Project coordination
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Writing
  • Administration

Demonstrate Research Ability

If you have completed a dissertation, thesis, research project, policy paper, academic publication, or professional research assignment, consider highlighting it.

Highlight French Proficiency

Because French is specifically identified as a desired skill, clearly state your level of French proficiency if applicable.

Connect Your Experience to Regional Integration

Your cover letter should explain why you are interested in regional integration and African economic transformation rather than simply stating that you need an internship.

Show Evidence of Impact

Whenever possible, describe what you achieved rather than simply listing responsibilities.

For example, instead of only saying that you “conducted research,” explain the type of research you conducted, what you analyzed, and how your findings were used.

Demonstrate Independence

Since ACET wants someone comfortable working with limited oversight, provide examples that demonstrate initiative and independent problem-solving.

Important Application Details

Detail Information
Organization African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET)
Position Regional Integration Graduate Intern
Program Regional Integration
Location Accra / Remote
Posted 13 August 2026
Minimum Education Postgraduate degree
Preferred Academic Background Economics or related Social Sciences
Key Skills Research, data analysis, writing, French, teamwork
Application Documents CV and Cover Letter
Application Email pnc@acetforafrica.org
Deadline Thursday, 27 August 2026
Interview Virtual or in person for candidates based in Ghana
Employment After Internship Not guaranteed

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications is Thursday, 27 August 2026.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to prepare and submit their applications before the final day rather than waiting until the deadline.

Late applications may not be considered.

Important Note for Applicants

ACET states that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

The organization also strongly encourages female candidates to apply.

Applicants should carefully review their CV and cover letter before submission to ensure that their qualifications and relevant experience are clearly presented.

Conclusion

The ACET Regional Integration Graduate Intern opportunity provides an interesting entry point for postgraduate graduates seeking practical experience in economic research, regional integration, public policy, international development, data analysis, stakeholder engagement, and African economic transformation.

The position goes beyond basic administrative internship duties. It combines research and data analysis with cross-country coordination, policy writing, stakeholder engagement, business development, and program support.

For candidates interested in careers in economic policy, research institutions, development organizations, consulting, government, regional organizations, or African development, the experience could provide valuable exposure to the type of work performed within a Pan-African economic policy institution.

Eligible applicants should prepare a targeted CV and compelling cover letter and submit both to pnc@acetforafrica.org before the Thursday, 27 August 2026 deadline.

Most importantly, applicants should demonstrate not only that they meet the academic requirements but also that they possess the research, analytical, writing, communication, organizational, and collaborative abilities required to contribute meaningfully to ACET’s Regional Integration Program.

item.content:encoded:
ESPN NEXT is ESPN’s structured early-career development program for people who want to build careers behind the scenes in sports media, content production, live events, digital storytelling, social media, and emerging platforms.

Rather than offering only a single short-term placement, ESPN NEXT is designed as a broader talent-development pathway. Participants may enter through Production Assistant opportunities, progress into Content Associate positions, participate in seasonal opportunities or internships, and potentially pursue additional leadership-development roles such as Peer Mentor, NEXT Trainer, and the selective NEXT Accelerator.

The program combines hands-on production experience, structured training, cross-platform exposure, professional development, and opportunities for increasing responsibility.

ESPN NEXT runs multiple hiring cycles throughout the year. These include January and July Production Assistant cohorts, Seasonal Production Assistant opportunities, and Fall, Spring, and Summer internships.

There is therefore no single annual application deadline for ESPN NEXT. Candidates need to monitor the relevant recruitment cycle and apply when the appropriate posting becomes available.

According to ESPN NEXT’s published hiring overview, upcoming recruitment windows include a Spring Internship posting in late September and a January Production Assistant posting in mid-October, while additional opportunities are generally advertised at other points throughout the year.

What Is ESPN NEXT?

ESPN NEXT is ESPN’s full-time early-career talent-development program.

Participants generally enter the full-time pathway as Production Assistants, gaining practical experience across ESPN’s content operations before potentially advancing into the Content Associate role.

The program develops early-career professionals working behind the scenes across several major areas of ESPN’s content ecosystem, including:

  • Studio programming
  • Live sporting events
  • Digital platforms
  • Social media
  • Emerging media platforms
  • Sports storytelling
  • Content production

The central goal is to train and develop the next generation of ESPN storytellers and producers.

ESPN NEXT combines real professional responsibility with structured development rather than separating training from day-to-day production work.

ESPN NEXT’s Approach to Early-Career Development

ESPN NEXT describes its approach as being built around several interconnected principles.

The program aims to give emerging professionals meaningful responsibility while providing the support necessary to develop their skills over time.

Its model emphasizes:

  • Practical experience
  • Structured training
  • Cross-platform learning
  • Ongoing feedback
  • Leadership development
  • Transparent career progression
  • Alignment with ESPN’s evolving content priorities

The aim is not simply to prepare participants for one specific production assignment but to help them develop the flexibility needed to contribute across different parts of ESPN.

Real Experience and Meaningful Responsibility

ESPN NEXT is built around the idea that future sports-media professionals develop most effectively when they are given real assignments.

Participants therefore gain hands-on exposure rather than relying entirely on classroom-style training.

Depending on their assignment, early-career professionals may gain experience supporting work connected with:

  • Studio shows
  • Live events
  • Digital content
  • Social media
  • Emerging platforms

This structure can help participants understand how sports stories are adapted for different audiences and formats.

Structured Training

Practical assignments are combined with structured learning opportunities.

Participants receive training intended to help them build the technical, professional, editorial, and collaborative capabilities needed to work successfully within ESPN’s content operations.

The program’s development model is intended to prepare participants for greater levels of responsibility as their careers progress.

Cross-Platform Exposure

A major feature of ESPN NEXT is its emphasis on platform fluency.

Modern sports-media professionals increasingly need to understand how content works across multiple channels rather than specializing immediately in a single medium.

Through cross-training, rotational experiences, and ongoing development, participants may gain exposure to ESPN’s:

  • Studio operations
  • Live-event production
  • Digital platforms
  • Social media operations

This cross-platform approach is intended to develop professionals who can adapt to changes in sports-media consumption and production.

ESPN NEXT’s Four Core Development Principles

1. Equitable Access and Opportunity

ESPN NEXT emphasizes fair and transparent hiring processes and data-driven placement.

The goal is to ensure that early-career professionals can enter ESPN with greater clarity about recruitment and development opportunities.

This approach is intended to create a structured route into sports-media careers rather than relying solely on informal networks or unclear career pathways.

2. Platform Fluency

Participants are developed to contribute across multiple media environments.

Through cross-training and rotational learning, they can build familiarity with different types of content production and distribution.

This can be particularly important as sports broadcasting increasingly overlaps with:

  • Social media
  • Streaming
  • Mobile content
  • Digital-first storytelling
  • Personalized content
  • Emerging technologies

3. Growth and Development

ESPN NEXT uses structured feedback and measurable development pathways.

The program also identifies individuals with leadership potential and creates opportunities for them to take on greater responsibility.

This can include progression to additional leadership opportunities within the NEXT ecosystem.

4. Business Partnership

The program works closely with ESPN business units.

This helps ESPN align the development of early-career talent with changing production requirements and content priorities.

Rather than operating separately from the company’s core activities, ESPN NEXT aims to build a pipeline that directly supports ESPN’s future workforce needs.

History of ESPN NEXT

The ESPN NEXT program has continued evolving since its launch.

July 2019: ESPN NEXT Launches

ESPN NEXT began in July 2019 with its first group of:

21 Production Assistants

This initial cohort marked the formal launch of the program and ESPN’s effort to create a more structured system for developing the next generation of sports storytellers.

September 2023: Expansion into Social and Digital

In September 2023, ESPN NEXT relaunched with a significant expansion into social and digital platforms.

This reflected broader changes within sports media and the growing importance of digital-first distribution.

Since that relaunch, ESPN NEXT Production Assistants and Content Associates have contributed to projects including:

  • SC+
  • SportsCenter For You

The expansion demonstrated the program’s increasing focus on preparing young professionals for a media environment extending well beyond traditional television.

January 2024: Accelerator Class Begins

The first NEXT Accelerator class launched in January 2024.

The Accelerator is a selective leadership-development experience focusing on:

  • Individual career development
  • Mentorship
  • Coaching
  • Strategic project experience

It creates an additional pathway for high-performing participants seeking to strengthen their leadership capabilities.

April 2026: NEXT.ESPN.com Goes Live

In April 2026, ESPN launched NEXT.ESPN.com as a dedicated digital hub for ESPN NEXT.

The platform is intended to provide ongoing access to:

  • Program information
  • Resources
  • Inspiration
  • Career opportunities
  • Early-career development information

This gives prospective applicants a central location for monitoring future opportunities.

ESPN NEXT Hiring Overview

ESPN NEXT uses structured hiring cycles throughout the year.

The program recruits full-time Production Assistants through cohort-based hiring while also offering seasonal roles and internship opportunities during different production periods.

The published schedule is a general hiring timeline, not necessarily a guaranteed application deadline for every individual posting.

Candidates should therefore monitor Disney Careers and ESPN NEXT when the relevant posting period approaches.

January Production Assistant Cycle

For candidates interested in joining ESPN NEXT early in the calendar year, the January Production Assistant cycle generally follows this timeline:

Job posting: Mid-October
Interviews: November
Offers: Early December
Start date: Mid-January

This means applicants interested in a January start should normally begin monitoring ESPN career pages by early or mid-October.

July Production Assistant Cycle

The July Production Assistant hiring cycle generally follows:

Job posting: Mid-March
Interviews: April
Offers: Mid-May
Start date: Mid-July

This cycle provides another annual entry point for full-time Production Assistant opportunities.

Seasonal Production Assistant Cycle

Seasonal Production Assistant roles are generally recruited according to the following schedule:

Job posting: Mid-May
Interviews: June
Offers: Early July
Start date: Early to mid-August

Seasonal positions help ESPN support periods of increased production demand.

Candidates interested in short-term or seasonal exposure to sports production should therefore begin monitoring opportunities during May.

Fall Internship Cycle

ESPN NEXT’s general timeline for Fall Internships is:

Job posting: Mid-June
Interviews: Mid-July
Offers: Mid-August
Start date: Early September

Applicants interested in fall opportunities should therefore begin searching well before the academic fall semester begins.

Spring Internship Cycle

The Spring Internship recruitment cycle generally follows:

Job posting: Late September
Interviews: Late October
Offers: Late November
Start date: Mid-January

For candidates planning ahead for early 2027, this is particularly relevant because Spring Internship postings are expected around late September 2026, based on the general ESPN NEXT timeline.

Applicants should remember that late September is the expected posting period, not necessarily the final application deadline.

The actual vacancy posting should be checked for the official deadline.

Summer Internship Cycle

ESPN NEXT’s general Summer Internship timeline is:

Job posting: January or early February
Interviews: Mid-March
Offers: Mid-to-late April
Start date: Early June

Summer internships are therefore recruited several months in advance.

Students hoping to participate in a summer program should not wait until late spring to begin looking for openings.

Understanding the Hiring Calendar

The ESPN NEXT recruitment calendar is valuable because it allows candidates to prepare before jobs are posted.

A useful planning sequence is:

  1. Identify which hiring cycle best matches your availability.
  2. Begin preparing your resume and portfolio before the posting window.
  3. Monitor ESPN NEXT and Disney Careers as the expected posting period approaches.
  4. Apply promptly once the opportunity becomes available.
  5. Prepare for the interview period indicated in the hiring calendar.
  6. Keep the expected offer and start dates in mind when planning school, employment, or relocation commitments.

ESPN NEXT Roles and Career Progression

The program includes several professional and leadership opportunities.

These positions are not necessarily independent entry points. Some become available after participants have already progressed within ESPN NEXT.

Production Assistant

The Production Assistant, or PA, is the principal entry point into the full-time ESPN NEXT program.

Production Assistants receive hands-on experience supporting content production across areas including:

  • Studio shows
  • Live events
  • Digital platforms
  • Social platforms

The Production Assistant position gives early-career professionals an opportunity to understand ESPN’s production systems while building practical storytelling and media-production capabilities.

Content Associate

The Content Associate, or CA, represents the next step in the ESPN NEXT progression pathway.

Content Associates are Production Assistants who have earned promotion within the program.

They take on:

  • Greater responsibility
  • More demanding assignments
  • Expanded production expectations

Progression is therefore built into the ESPN NEXT structure rather than treating the Production Assistant position as an isolated experience.

Peer Mentor

Content Associates may have an opportunity to serve as Peer Mentors.

Peer Mentors help support newly hired Production Assistants.

Through this role, participants can develop skills related to:

  • Mentoring
  • Leadership
  • Feedback
  • Team support
  • Professional communication

It also allows more experienced participants to contribute to the development of incoming cohorts.

NEXT Trainer

Experienced ESPN NEXT participants may also serve as NEXT Trainers.

NEXT Trainers support:

  • New-hire onboarding
  • Foundational training
  • Early professional development

This gives experienced participants an opportunity to practice facilitation and leadership while contributing to the broader program.

NEXT Accelerator

The NEXT Accelerator is a selective leadership-development opportunity available to high-performing participants.

The program focuses on:

  • Mentorship
  • Coaching
  • Individual career development
  • Strategic project experience

It is intended for participants demonstrating strong potential for future leadership.

ESPN NEXT Career Path

A simplified pathway can be understood as:

Production Assistant → Content Associate → Expanded leadership and development opportunities

Potential leadership opportunities may include:

  • Peer Mentor
  • NEXT Trainer
  • NEXT Accelerator

Individual progression will depend on performance, available opportunities, and ESPN’s staffing and business needs.

Sports Storytelling at the Center of the Program

While ESPN NEXT includes structured career development, its central mission remains sports storytelling.

Participants are being prepared to contribute to how ESPN tells stories across an increasingly diverse media landscape.

That means understanding not only the sport itself but also:

  • Audience behavior
  • Digital formats
  • Social storytelling
  • Live-event production
  • Studio production
  • Emerging content formats

ESPN’s long-term objective is to develop storytellers and producers capable of growing with the company as sports-media consumption continues evolving.

Who Should Consider ESPN NEXT?

The program is designed for early-career talent interested in behind-the-scenes sports media and content production.

It may appeal particularly to people interested in:

  • Sports media
  • Broadcasting
  • Production
  • Digital content
  • Social media
  • Live events
  • Sports storytelling
  • Emerging platforms
  • Content development

The source information provided does not list universal degree, age, citizenship, major, work-authorization, or experience requirements applying to every ESPN NEXT opening.

These requirements may vary by individual vacancy.

Candidates should therefore review each Disney Careers job posting carefully rather than assuming eligibility based solely on the general program description.

How to Prepare for ESPN NEXT Opportunities

Because ESPN NEXT follows relatively predictable recruitment periods, candidates can prepare strategically.

1. Select the Right Hiring Cycle

Determine whether you are primarily interested in:

  • Full-time Production Assistant opportunities
  • Seasonal Production Assistant positions
  • Fall internships
  • Spring internships
  • Summer internships

Then work backward from the expected posting date.

2. Prepare Your Resume Early

Do not wait until a vacancy appears.

A strong early-career sports-media resume might highlight relevant experience in areas such as:

  • Video production
  • Sports journalism
  • Digital storytelling
  • Social media
  • Campus media
  • Broadcasting
  • Editing
  • Live production
  • Content creation

Only include experience you actually have.

3. Build a Portfolio Where Relevant

If the individual posting requests or permits work samples, candidates may benefit from organizing relevant examples ahead of time.

These might include:

  • Video work
  • Sports stories
  • Social-media content
  • Editing projects
  • Production projects
  • Digital packages

Candidates should follow the requirements of each actual posting.

4. Learn ESPN’s Platforms

Because ESPN NEXT emphasizes platform fluency, applicants should understand how ESPN tells sports stories differently across:

  • Television
  • Digital
  • Social
  • Live-event environments

This does not replace professional skills, but it can help candidates understand the organization they are applying to join.

5. Be Prepared to Discuss Sports Storytelling

Applicants should be prepared to explain:

  • Why sports media interests them
  • What makes effective sports storytelling
  • How audiences consume sports differently across platforms
  • What skills they hope to develop

6. Monitor Recruitment Windows

item.content:encoded:
Boston Consulting Group is recruiting a Senior Analyst – BCG Vantage to join its Social Impact Practice Area in Gurgaon, Haryana, India. The full-time position is designed for experienced professionals with deep expertise in education and skilling, particularly candidates who have worked across K–12 education, higher education, technical and vocational education and training, government transformation programmes, donor-funded initiatives, or consulting.

The role sits on BCG Vantage’s Client Focus path and combines sector expertise, consulting-style problem solving, client engagement, research and analysis, business development, knowledge creation, and support to project teams delivering large-scale education and skilling transformations.

Boston Consulting Group is seeking candidates with approximately 4–6 years of relevant industry experience, while consulting experience is strongly preferred. A bachelor’s degree is required, and an advanced degree is considered advantageous.

The position is based in Gurgaon and will involve direct interaction with clients, BCG Project Leaders, Associates, Consultants, global topic leaders, and other colleagues across the firm. Travel to client locations is expected when required to deliver projects and workshops.

The vacancy is listed under BCG’s Expertise and Insights category with Job ID 58923.

No specific application closing date is stated in the information provided. Interested applicants should therefore consider applying as early as possible while the vacancy remains open.

About Boston Consulting Group

Boston Consulting Group, widely known as BCG, is a global management consulting firm that works with leaders across business, government, and society to address complex challenges and identify opportunities for transformation and growth.

Founded in 1963, BCG was an early pioneer of business strategy consulting. Its work has since expanded considerably beyond traditional strategy.

Today, BCG supports organisations with areas including:

  • Business transformation
  • Corporate strategy
  • Digital transformation
  • Technology
  • Organisational change
  • Competitive advantage
  • Innovation
  • Corporate ventures
  • Public-sector transformation
  • Social impact
  • Sustainability
  • Data and analytics
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Organisational purpose

BCG emphasizes the combination of human expertise with digital capabilities and works through multidisciplinary teams that bring together sector knowledge, functional expertise, analytical capabilities, and technology.

The Senior Analyst position in Gurgaon forms part of this wider model while concentrating specifically on the education and skilling sector within BCG’s Social Impact Practice Area.

About the Senior Analyst – BCG Vantage Role

The Senior Analyst – BCG Vantage position is intended for someone who can bring specialist education-sector knowledge into BCG client work.

The successful candidate will work as part of a growing global team and contribute expertise to consulting engagements, proposals, workshops, knowledge development, and business-development initiatives.

The position is not limited to desk-based research.

The role has a strong client-facing element, and candidates should be comfortable using their subject expertise to help BCG teams develop practical solutions to complex education and workforce-development challenges.

The successful analyst will contribute both independently and through BCG Vantage assets and institutional knowledge.

What Is BCG Vantage?

Within the context of this position, BCG Vantage brings specialised knowledge and expertise into client-facing consulting work.

The Senior Analyst will work on the Client Focus path, meaning the role involves close engagement with consulting teams and clients.

Rather than serving solely as a background researcher, the Senior Analyst is expected to contribute directly to:

  • Client cases
  • Proposals
  • Workshops
  • Research
  • Analysis
  • Commercialisation activities
  • Knowledge products
  • Intellectual property
  • Training and onboarding
  • Business development

The successful candidate will therefore need both deep sector expertise and the ability to translate that knowledge into practical client solutions.

Focus on Education and Skilling

The position is located within BCG’s Social Impact Practice Area and focuses heavily on education and skills development.

The selected Senior Analyst may work across several major areas.

K–12 Education

The role may involve projects related to school education.

Examples specifically mentioned in the job description include:

  • Early Childhood Care and Education
  • AI and education
  • Assessment-to-action approaches
  • Exemplar schools
  • School-to-work transition
  • Secondary education reforms

This means candidates with experience designing, implementing, evaluating, or advising large-scale school-system reforms may be particularly relevant.

Early Childhood Care and Education

Early Childhood Care and Education, or ECCE, is specifically identified as an area within the position.

Candidates who have worked on early-learning systems, preschool education, early childhood policy, programme implementation, learning outcomes, or education-system transformation may be able to contribute this experience to BCG projects.

Artificial Intelligence and Education

The role also mentions AI x Education.

This reflects BCG’s interest in the rapidly expanding role of artificial intelligence in education systems.

The successful candidate may contribute to discussions or projects around how AI can be used within educational systems, programmes, institutional transformation, assessments, learning environments, or education delivery.

Candidates are additionally expected to be comfortable using AI tools themselves.

Assessment to Action

Assessment is another area identified in the job description.

This can involve translating data about student performance and system outcomes into practical interventions, implementation strategies, or policy improvements.

The Senior Analyst may therefore need to help clients move beyond data collection toward evidence-based decision-making.

Exemplar Schools

The position also mentions exemplar-school approaches.

This may involve supporting education systems in understanding, designing, evaluating, or scaling high-performing school models.

School-to-Work Transition

The transition from education to employment is a significant component of education and skilling policy.

Candidates may bring experience related to:

  • Employability
  • Career pathways
  • Workforce readiness
  • Skills development
  • Vocational education
  • Industry engagement
  • Youth employment
  • Labour-market transitions

Secondary Education Reforms

Large-scale reforms affecting secondary education are another possible area of work.

Relevant expertise could include policy development, institutional reform, curriculum change, implementation, learning outcomes, government programmes, or transformation initiatives.

Higher Education Work

The Senior Analyst may also contribute to higher-education projects.

BCG specifically references:

  • Greenfield establishment
  • Brownfield transformation

Greenfield Higher Education Development

Greenfield work generally involves creating or designing new institutions, programmes, or systems.

In a higher-education context, this could involve helping clients think through the development of new universities, institutions, programmes, operating models, or education ecosystems.

Brownfield Transformation

Brownfield transformation concerns improving or redesigning existing systems and institutions.

This may involve areas such as:

  • Institutional strategy
  • Academic transformation
  • Operating models
  • Digitalisation
  • Organisational reform
  • Student outcomes
  • Governance
  • Performance improvement

Candidates with experience in higher-education transformation may therefore be particularly relevant.

Technical and Vocational Education and Training

The job also places significant emphasis on skilling.

Relevant areas mentioned include:

  • ITI transformation
  • Short-term skilling
  • TVET
  • Workforce-development programmes

Technical and Vocational Education and Training is particularly important for candidates who have worked at the intersection of education policy, skills development, employment, government programmes, and industry needs.

Applicants with experience working on large-scale workforce-development initiatives may have a strong fit.

Government Experience Is Highly Relevant

BCG particularly values candidates who have experience working with government.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Education policy
  • Programme design
  • Programme implementation
  • Multi-year transformation programmes
  • Public-sector reform
  • State-level education initiatives
  • Ministry-level programmes
  • Education-system strengthening

BCG’s education practice has worked on large-scale transformation projects with state governments and ministries in India.

Candidates who understand the complexity of working within public-sector environments may therefore be particularly competitive.

Experience with Donor-Funded Programmes

The job description also specifically highlights experience with donor-funded programmes.

Examples of development institutions mentioned include:

  • Asian Development Bank
  • World Bank

Candidates who have worked with multilateral development institutions, donors, governments, development agencies, or internationally financed education programmes may therefore have relevant experience.

This could include roles related to:

  • Programme implementation
  • Policy advisory work
  • Monitoring and evaluation
  • Research
  • Technical assistance
  • Sector reform
  • Education financing
  • Institutional strengthening

BCG’s Social Impact Practice

BCG describes social impact as central to the firm’s work and values.

The firm works with:

  • Social-sector organisations
  • Public-sector institutions
  • Private-sector organisations

to develop solutions intended to create positive societal impact.

Within education, BCG works across the sector value chain.

Its projects have included:

  • School education
  • Higher education
  • Skills development
  • Government education transformation
  • Private-sector education
  • Public-sector education
  • Workforce development

BCG states that globally it has undertaken more than 500 projects in the education sector across public and private sectors.

The Senior Analyst will therefore enter an established education practice rather than building the firm’s education expertise from the beginning.

Key Responsibilities

The successful Senior Analyst will undertake a broad range of responsibilities.

Contribute to Client Cases

The analyst will work directly on consulting engagements.

This can involve:

  • Conducting analysis
  • Developing insights
  • Providing sector expertise
  • Supporting solution design
  • Developing recommendations
  • Preparing client deliverables

The objective is to help case teams create significant impact for clients.

Support Proposals

The analyst will also contribute to proposals for potential client engagements.

This may involve:

  • Conducting background research
  • Developing sector insights
  • Preparing analytical material
  • Supporting proposal narratives
  • Identifying potential solutions
  • Developing relevant knowledge assets

Strong proposal-development skills can therefore be valuable.

Participate in Client Workshops

The role involves contributing to client workshops.

This requires the ability to communicate complex education and skilling issues clearly and confidently.

Candidates should be comfortable interacting with senior stakeholders and adapting their communication style to different audiences.

Travel to Clients

Travel is expected.

The Senior Analyst may need to travel to client sites to support cases, workshops, implementation, or other project activities.

Candidates should therefore be comfortable with a consulting environment in which project requirements can involve travel.

Support Commercialisation

The Senior Analyst will work with business leaders to support BCG’s commercialisation efforts within the relevant sector or topic.

This includes contributing analysis and expertise to:

  • Proposals
  • Client workshops
  • Marketing materials
  • Business-development activities

The successful candidate should therefore understand both the intellectual and commercial dimensions of consulting.

Develop Intellectual Property

The role includes developing intellectual property and assets for BCG.

These knowledge resources may include:

  • Research tools
  • Databases
  • Frameworks
  • Case vignettes
  • Proposal repositories
  • Analytical models
  • Sector knowledge products

The successful analyst will help turn individual project experience into reusable institutional knowledge.

Support Junior Colleagues

The Senior Analyst is also expected to contribute to the onboarding and development of junior colleagues.

This may involve sharing sector expertise, providing guidance, explaining methodologies, and supporting internal capability building.

Required Professional Experience

BCG is looking for candidates with:

4–6 years of industry experience in education and skilling.

Consulting experience is:

Strongly preferred.

This is therefore not primarily an entry-level position.

Candidates should already have several years of substantive experience and should be able to demonstrate expertise rather than general interest in education.

Relevant experience could come from:

  • Consulting firms
  • Government
  • Ministries
  • Development agencies
  • International financial institutions
  • Donor-funded programmes
  • Education organisations
  • Skills-development programmes
  • Research institutions
  • Public-policy organisations
  • NGOs
  • Education companies

Educational Qualifications

A:

Bachelor’s degree is required.

An:

Advanced degree is preferred.

An advanced degree could therefore strengthen an application, particularly where it supports expertise in education, economics, public policy, development, business, social sciences, or another related area.

However, the job description does not state that a master’s or doctoral degree is mandatory.

English Language Requirement

Applicants need excellent:

  • Written English
  • Verbal English

The job requires English at a proficiency level.

Strong communication skills are particularly important because the analyst will need to:

  • Write client-ready materials
  • Participate in stakeholder discussions
  • Conduct workshops
  • Work with global colleagues
  • Communicate complex ideas clearly

AI Skills

BCG specifically expects the Senior Analyst to be:

Fluent in using AI tools.

Applicants should also demonstrate:

  • Curiosity about AI
  • Willingness to experiment with AI tools
  • Ability to use AI to create additional client value

This requirement reflects the growing importance of AI within both consulting and education transformation.

Candidates should be able to demonstrate practical familiarity with AI rather than simply stating an abstract interest in the technology.

Stakeholder Management

The successful candidate must be able to manage complex stakeholder conversations.

This is particularly important in education projects involving:

  • Governments
  • Ministries
  • Donors
  • Education institutions
  • Consultants
  • Development partners
  • Senior executives
  • Public-sector officials

Projects may include stakeholders with different priorities and expectations.

The Senior Analyst must therefore communicate diplomatically while maintaining analytical clarity and project momentum.

Fast-Paced Working Environment

Candidates should be able to operate in an environment requiring:

  • Rapid turnaround
  • Flexibility
  • Prioritisation
  • Ownership
  • Adaptability
  • Independent execution

BCG describes the environment as fast-changing and complex.

Applicants should be comfortable working with ambiguity while maintaining the quality of their deliverables.

Growth Mindset and Learning Adaptability

BCG is looking for individuals who can perform in challenging situations and continue adapting.

A growth mindset is particularly important because consulting projects often expose professionals to:

  • New topics
  • New clients
  • New countries
  • New stakeholders
  • New methods
  • Tight deadlines

The ability to learn quickly and adjust effectively is therefore central to the role.

Client-Facing Skills

Candidates should be comfortable working directly with demanding internal and external clients.

The Senior Analyst should be able to:

  • Build professional relationships
  • Understand client needs
  • Communicate effectively
  • Maintain a service-oriented mindset
  • Adapt to project circumstances
  • Deliver high-quality work

The role requires confidence without sacrificing collaboration.

Communication with Senior Stakeholders

The Senior Analyst may interact with senior client stakeholders.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate the ability to:

  • Structure complex ideas
  • Present evidence clearly
  • Explain recommendations
  • Engage audiences
  • Respond to questions
  • Navigate disagreement professionally

Strong executive communication will be valuable.

Designing High-Impact Solutions

The job description emphasizes applying deep education and skilling expertise to client problems.

Solutions should account for what is:

  • Desirable
  • Feasible
  • Viable on the ground

This distinction is important.

The role is not simply about producing theoretically strong policy ideas. Candidates must think about whether those solutions can realistically be implemented within the institutional, financial, political, and operational environment.

Client-Ready Deliverables

Successful candidates should be able to produce high-quality materials including:

  • Memos
  • Presentations
  • Documents
  • Analytical materials
  • Client reports

Deliverables should be:

  • Structured
  • Clear
  • Visually engaging
  • Adapted to the client’s context

Strong PowerPoint-style communication and structured writing are therefore likely to be valuable skills.

Knowledge Asset Development

The Senior Analyst will contribute to developing BCG’s internal knowledge resources.

Examples mentioned include:

  • Tools
  • Databases
  • Case vignettes
  • Proposal repositories

The ability to organise information systematically and transform project experience into reusable knowledge will be valuable.

Ownership and Autonomy

Candidates are expected to show strong ownership of their work.

This includes the ability to:

  • Generate high-quality outputs
  • Work entrepreneurially
  • Prioritise effectively
  • Discuss priorities transparently
  • Execute independently
  • Manage competing demands

The Senior Analyst will work within teams but should not require constant direction.

Working in Agile Environments

The position requires flexibility.

Candidates should be comfortable working in:

  • Changing circumstances
  • Complex situations
  • Fast-moving client environments
  • Ambiguous settings

BCG specifically values curiosity, creativity, and openness to new ideas.

Who You Will Work With

The Senior Analyst will interact with several groups across BCG.

These include:

  • Clients
  • BCG Project Leaders
  • Associates
  • Consultants
  • Global topic leaders
  • Other BCG Vantage colleagues

During active cases, the analyst may work closely with consulting teams and clients.

Between cases, the analyst may collaborate with global topic leaders and colleagues across BCG to build capabilities, develop knowledge, and support future client work.

Work Location

The position is based in:

Gurgaon, Haryana, India

Gurgaon, also widely known as Gurugram, is one of India’s major corporate and consulting hubs and forms part of the wider Delhi National Capital Region.

Candidates should therefore be prepared to work from the relevant BCG office and travel as required for client engagements.

Employment Type

The position is:

Full-time

It is classified under:

Expertise and Insights

The official BCG Job ID is:

58923

Application Deadline

The information provided does not specify a formal application deadline.

The role was listed as open for applications, but applicants should not assume it will remain available indefinitely.

BCG may close recruitment after identifying an appropriate candidate or reaching the desired application volume.

Prospective candidates should therefore consider applying as soon as possible.

How to Apply

Candidates can apply through Boston Consulting Group’s official careers platform.

Position: Senior Analyst – BCG Vantage
Job ID: 58923
Location: Gurgaon, Haryana, India

APPLY HERE

Applicants should ensure that their CV clearly demonstrates relevant education and skilling expertise before submitting.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

1. Make Your Education Expertise Obvious

This role is not looking for a generalist analyst who happens to be interested in education.

Applicants should show meaningful expertise in areas such as:

  • K–12
  • Higher education
  • TVET
  • Skilling
  • Education reform
  • Education policy
  • Government programmes

Place this expertise prominently in your CV.

2. Quantify Large-Scale Transformation Experience

Where possible, specify:

  • Number of schools involved
  • Number of learners reached
  • Geographic coverage
  • Programme budgets
  • Government agencies supported
  • Years of implementation
  • Measurable outcomes

Numbers make the scale of your experience easier to understand.

3. Highlight Government Experience

If you have worked with:

  • Ministries
  • State governments
  • Public agencies
  • Regulators

make this clear.

BCG specifically values government experience.

4. Highlight Donor-Funded Work

Experience with organisations such as:

  • World Bank
  • Asian Development Bank
  • Other multilateral development organisations

should be clearly identified.

Explain the programme, your responsibilities, and the impact you helped deliver.

5. Demonstrate Consulting Skills

Candidates with consulting experience should highlight:

  • Client engagement
  • Problem solving
  • Proposal development
  • Workshop facilitation
  • Executive communication
  • Structured analysis
  • Slide preparation
  • Project delivery

6. Show Practical AI Capability

Do not simply write “AI” under a skills section.

Where possible, demonstrate how you have used AI tools to:

  • Conduct research
  • Analyse information
  • Improve productivity
  • Develop insights
  • Create client outputs

7. Highlight Stakeholder Management

Provide examples showing that you have successfully worked across:

  • Government
  • Donors

  • Educational institutions
  • Senior executives
  • Technical experts

8. Demonstrate Results

BCG will likely be more interested in what your work achieved than simply what tasks you performed.

Instead of writing:

“Supported education programme implementation”

consider something more specific, such as:

“Supported implementation of a multi-year secondary education transformation programme across X districts, coordinating government and programme stakeholders.”

Why Consider This BCG Opportunity?

This position offers experienced education professionals an opportunity to combine sector expertise with high-level consulting and social impact work.

The role provides exposure to:

  • Large-scale education transformations
  • Government clients
  • Donor programmes
  • Global BCG expertise
  • Strategic consulting
  • AI-enabled problem solving
  • Knowledge development
  • Public-sector reform
  • Client-facing advisory work

For professionals who have already built expertise in education and want to apply it to complex, large-scale transformation programmes, the position provides an opportunity to work at the intersection of strategy, education, skills development, public policy, and social impact.

Conclusion

The Senior Analyst – BCG Vantage position in Gurgaon, India is a strong opportunity for experienced education and skilling professionals seeking to join Boston Consulting Group’s Social Impact Practice Area.

Candidates should bring approximately 4–6 years of experience in education and skilling, with consulting experience strongly preferred.

BCG is particularly interested in professionals with expertise across:

  • K–12 education
  • Higher education
  • TVET
  • Skills development
  • Government transformation
  • Education policy

Strong English communication, AI-tool proficiency, stakeholder-management ability, adaptability, client-facing confidence, and the ability to produce high-quality analytical work are also important.

The Senior Analyst will work directly with clients and BCG consulting teams, contribute to proposals and workshops, build intellectual property, support business development, and help develop education solutions that are both strategically compelling and practical to implement.

The role is full-time and based in Gurgaon, Haryana, India, with travel expected for client work.
