item.content:encoded:
The University of British Columbia (UBC) Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is set to open applications for the Winter 2027 intake, providing eligible young Africans with an opportunity to pursue selected master’s degree programmes at one of Canada’s leading universities.

Applications for the Winter 2027 intake will open on August 31, 2026. The opportunity is designed for talented African students and refugees who demonstrate strong academic potential, transformative leadership, community service, and a commitment to contributing to the development of their home countries.

The program is offered through UBC’s Vancouver campus and is available only for applicants seeking admission to a specific list of eligible master’s degree programmes within the Faculty of Land and Food Systems, Faculty of Forestry, and Faculty of Science.

For prospective applicants, the application process involves several stages. Interested candidates must first identify an eligible programme, submit an expression of interest, complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application if invited, and subsequently apply to the relevant UBC faculty.

UBC Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program 2027 Overview

The Winter 2027 opportunity is intended for qualified African applicants who want to pursue graduate-level studies at the University of British Columbia.

The program places considerable emphasis not only on academic achievement but also on leadership, community engagement, and the potential contribution an applicant can make to the development of their home country.

Successful candidates must therefore demonstrate a combination of:

  • Strong academic performance.
  • Leadership potential and a record of service.
  • Commitment to their communities.
  • A clear connection between their proposed studies and development priorities.
  • Potential to contribute meaningfully to the development of their home country.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to African graduates seeking advanced training in areas related to food and resource economics, food science, forestry, sustainable forest management, urban forestry, geomatics, and data science.

When Will Applications Open?

Applications for the Winter 2027 intake open on August 31, 2026.

However, applicants should understand that the opening date is not the only important date in the application process. The opportunity follows a multi-stage process, with different deadlines for the expression of interest, Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application, and subsequent UBC faculty application.

Applicants should therefore begin preparing their documents before applications officially open.

Who Can Apply for the UBC Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program?

To be considered for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Masters’ Degree Program at UBC, applicants must satisfy the program’s eligibility requirements.

Applicants must:

  • Have completed a Bachelor’s degree.
  • Not already hold a Master’s degree.
  • Be 35 years old or younger at the time of application, meaning applicants must have been born in 1990 or after.
  • Be a citizen or refugee of an African country.
  • Be applying for a master’s degree in one of the programmes specifically identified as eligible under the program.
  • Meet the minimum academic requirements for the selected UBC graduate programme.

Meeting the basic eligibility requirements does not automatically guarantee selection. Candidates will also be assessed based on academic merit, leadership, community service, the quality of their application, alignment with the program theme, and their potential development impact.

Eligible Master’s Degree Programmes at UBC

One of the most important aspects of the Winter 2027 opportunity is that applicants cannot apply to any master’s programme at UBC through this particular program.

The opportunity is restricted to the following programmes.

Faculty of Land and Food Systems

Applicants interested in the Faculty of Land and Food Systems may apply for:

  • Master of Food and Resource Economics (MFRE)
  • Master of Food Science (MFS)

These programmes may be particularly relevant to candidates whose academic and professional interests relate to food systems, agriculture, economics, food production, resource management, and sustainable development.

Faculty of Forestry

The following programmes are available under the Faculty of Forestry:

  • Master of Sustainable Forest Management (MSFM)
  • Master of International Forestry (MIF)
  • Master of Urban Forestry Leadership (MUFL)
  • Master of Geomatics for Environmental Management (MGEM)
  • Master of Science/Master of Applied Science in Forestry (Thesis-based)

These programmes provide potential pathways for applicants interested in forests, environmental management, natural resources, sustainability, climate-related challenges, conservation, urban forestry, and related areas.

Faculty of Science

The eligible programme under the Faculty of Science is:

  • Master of Data Science

The programme may be particularly suitable for applicants with interests or academic backgrounds related to data, analytics, computing, quantitative research, technology, and evidence-based decision-making.

Applicants should carefully review the academic requirements of their chosen programme before submitting an expression of interest.

UBC Academic Requirements and International Credentials

Applicants must satisfy UBC’s minimum academic requirements for the graduate programme they intend to pursue.

Because applicants will be applying from different African countries and may hold qualifications from different education systems, UBC provides information on minimum academic requirements and international credentials by country.

Prospective applicants should therefore verify that their Bachelor’s qualification meets the relevant academic standard for admission to their selected UBC programme.

This is an important step because eligibility for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program does not replace the academic admission requirements of the relevant UBC faculty.

Applicants should confirm their academic eligibility before proceeding with the application.

English Language Requirements

Applicants whose Bachelor’s degree was not taught in English may need to take an English proficiency examination.

Depending on their circumstances, applicants may be required to submit results from an approved English proficiency examination such as:

  • TOEFL
  • IELTS

Applicants should verify UBC’s current English language requirements and determine whether their previous education satisfies the university’s requirements.

Those who need an English proficiency examination should plan ahead so that their results can be available when required during the application process.

Step 1: Decide on Your Programme of Interest

The first major step is to identify the UBC master’s programme you wish to pursue.

Applicants should carefully review the list of eligible programmes and select a programme that:

  1. Matches their academic background.
  2. Meets their professional and career objectives.
  3. Meets the eligibility requirements of the relevant UBC faculty.
  4. Aligns with their leadership and development goals.
  5. Is specifically included among the programmes supported by the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at UBC.

Applicants should not assume that every graduate programme offered by UBC is eligible under this opportunity.

Step 2: Submit an Expression of Interest

After identifying an eligible programme, applicants must submit an expression of interest.

The deadline for submitting the expression of interest is September 6, 2026.

There are two expression-of-interest streams.

General Stream

The General Stream is intended for interested candidates who are not applying as refugees.

Applicants can submit their expression of interest through the UBC application form provided for the General Stream:

UBC General Stream Expression of Interest

Refugee and Displaced Persons Stream

Applicants applying as refugees or displaced persons should use the dedicated Refugee and Displaced Persons Stream:

UBC Refugee and Displaced Persons Expression of Interest

Applicants should ensure that they use the appropriate stream when submitting their expression of interest.

Step 3: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program Application

After the expression-of-interest stage, eligible applicants will be invited to proceed to the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application.

The invitation period for Round 1 is scheduled for September 15–30, 2026.

Not everyone who submits an expression of interest will necessarily proceed to this stage. Candidates who are identified as eligible will receive instructions on how to complete the next stage of the process.

The selection process considers several factors.

Academic Merit

Applicants must demonstrate academic ability sufficient to qualify for admission to their chosen UBC programme.

Strong academic performance is therefore an important component of the application.

Transformative Leadership and Community Service

Applicants are also assessed on their track record as transformative leaders and their service to their communities.

This means candidates should be able to demonstrate how they have used their knowledge, skills, experience, or leadership to contribute positively to others.

Community involvement can be an important part of demonstrating this criterion.

Quality and Relevance of the Application

The quality of the application is another key consideration.

Applicants should provide thoughtful, clear, authentic, and well-structured responses to the questions in the application form. Personal statements should directly address what is being asked rather than providing lengthy or unrelated information.

Potential Development Impact

The selection process also considers the potential impact of the applicant on the development of their home country.

Applicants should therefore be able to communicate how their proposed graduate studies can contribute to meaningful development outcomes after completing their education.

Documents Required for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program Application

Applicants invited to submit the full Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application should prepare the required documentation carefully.

The application is expected to include:

  • A completed Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application form.
  • Personal statements responding to the questions provided.
  • A CV or resume.
  • Two reference letters on official letterhead.
  • Academic transcripts.

The reference letters should be attached to the application as instructed. Applicants are specifically advised not to email the reference letters separately.

Personal Statements

The personal statements are an important component of the application.

Applicants should answer each question succinctly while ensuring that their responses demonstrate their experiences, aspirations, leadership, community engagement, and development goals.

Rather than simply listing achievements, applicants should explain the significance of their experiences and how those experiences have shaped their goals.

CV or Resume

Applicants should submit a clear and relevant CV or resume highlighting their:

  • Academic background.
  • Professional experience.
  • Leadership roles.
  • Community service.
  • Volunteer activities.
  • Relevant projects.
  • Awards or recognitions.
  • Skills and achievements.

The CV should complement rather than duplicate the information presented in the personal statements.

Reference Letters

Applicants are required to provide two reference letters on official letterhead.

Applicants should select referees who can provide meaningful information about their academic abilities, leadership qualities, character, community engagement, professional potential, or other relevant attributes.

The letters should be attached to the application as required rather than sent separately by email.

Academic Transcripts

Applicants must also provide their academic transcripts.

Candidates should ensure that the submitted academic documents are accurate and meet the requirements of the application process.

Step 4: Apply to the UBC Faculty

Applicants who successfully complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application stage will receive instructions on how to proceed with the UBC faculty application.

The second round of the application process is scheduled for November 1–20, 2026.

This stage is extremely important because successful candidates must also complete the relevant UBC faculty application.

UBC Faculty Application Deadline

The deadline for submitting the faculty application is November 20, 2026.

UBC has indicated that late applications will not be considered.

Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final day to submit their application. Completing the process early can provide time to identify and resolve any issues with documents, application forms, or other requirements.

Possible Application Fee Waiver

Some applicants may be eligible for an application fee waiver.

According to the application information, applicants whose citizenship and correspondence address are located in one of the world’s 50 least developed countries, according to the United Nations classification, may be eligible for a fee waiver.

Applicants should check the relevant list to determine whether their country qualifies.

For applicants whose country is not included on the relevant list, UBC indicates that they may request a fee waiver when submitting their Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application package.

If an applicant is subsequently invited to the Faculty Application stage, instructions will be provided on how to use the fee waiver during the application process.

Applicants should pay particular attention to this process because submitting an application without requesting or applying the applicable fee waiver may mean that a refund cannot subsequently be provided.

Important Application Dates for Winter 2027

Prospective applicants should keep track of all the important dates because the application process involves several stages.

Application Stage Date
Winter 2027 applications open August 31, 2026
Expression of interest deadline September 6, 2026
Invitation period for eligible applicants September 15–30, 2026
UBC Faculty application period November 1–20, 2026
Final faculty application deadline November 20, 2026

The dates above are particularly important because missing an earlier stage may prevent an applicant from progressing to the next stage.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Competition for highly sought-after graduate opportunities can be significant. Applicants should therefore begin preparing well before the relevant deadlines.

1. Select the Right Programme

Do not select a programme simply because it is available.

Applicants should consider whether the programme genuinely fits their academic history, professional experience, career plans, and long-term development objectives.

2. Verify Your Academic Eligibility

Check the minimum academic requirements for your country and intended UBC programme.

This should be done before submitting the expression of interest.

3. Develop a Clear Leadership Story

The program considers transformative leadership and community service.

Applicants should identify specific examples demonstrating how they have:

  • Led an initiative.
  • Solved a community problem.
  • Mobilised people or resources.
  • Supported vulnerable groups.
  • Created positive change.
  • Contributed to an organisation or community.
  • Demonstrated initiative in challenging circumstances.

Specific examples are generally more persuasive than broad claims about being a leader.

4. Connect Your Education to Development

Applicants should clearly articulate why their chosen master’s programme matters.

A strong application should establish a logical connection between:

Past experience → proposed programme → skills to be gained → future contribution → development impact.

This can help demonstrate the applicant’s potential contribution to their home country.

5. Prepare Your References Early

Because two reference letters are required, applicants should identify appropriate referees well before the deadline.

Giving referees sufficient time can help ensure that the letters are thoughtful, relevant, and submitted in the required format.

6. Review Your Personal Statements Carefully

Personal statements should answer the specific questions asked in the application.

Applicants should avoid generic responses and ensure that their statements clearly communicate their experiences, motivation, leadership, community engagement, academic goals, and future aspirations.

7. Prepare Academic Documents

Applicants should ensure that transcripts and other academic documents are available before they begin the application process.

If documents need to be translated, certified, or obtained from an institution, applicants should allow additional time.

8. Check English Language Requirements

Applicants whose Bachelor’s degree was not taught in English should determine whether they need TOEFL, IELTS, or another accepted English proficiency assessment.

Taking the test early can prevent delays later in the process.

APPLY HERE

Why Applicants Should Pay Attention to the Multi-Stage Process

A major feature of the UBC Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application is that it is not a single-step application.

Candidates first express their interest. Eligible applicants may then be invited to complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application. Successful candidates subsequently receive instructions for applying to their UBC faculty.

This means applicants should carefully monitor their email and follow every instruction provided by UBC.

Missing an invitation, failing to submit a required document, or overlooking a subsequent faculty application deadline could affect an applicant’s ability to proceed.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be particularly relevant to African graduates who have completed a Bachelor’s degree and want to pursue advanced studies in one of the specified fields at UBC.

Strong candidates are likely to be individuals who can demonstrate both academic readiness and a meaningful record of leadership or service.

The opportunity may therefore appeal to applicants with backgrounds in areas such as:

  • Agriculture and food systems.
  • Food science.
  • Economics and resource management.
  • Forestry.
  • Environmental management.
  • Natural resource management.
  • Urban forestry.
  • Geomatics.
  • Data science.
  • Sustainability and development.

However, applicants must still satisfy the specific academic and programme requirements of their chosen UBC degree.

Where to Submit the Expression of Interest

Applicants should use the official UBC application channels corresponding to their applicant category.

General Stream:
Submit the General Stream Expression of Interest

Refugee and Displaced Persons Stream:
Submit the Refugee and Displaced Persons Expression of Interest

Applicants should carefully read the official instructions before submitting any information.

Visit HERE for more information about the UBC Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program 2027.

Application Deadline

The first major deadline is September 6, 2026, when expressions of interest must be submitted.

Applicants who progress through the selection process will then have additional deadlines to meet, including the UBC Faculty application period from November 1 to November 20, 2026.

The final faculty application deadline is November 20, 2026, and late applications will not be considered.

Because the process begins with an expression of interest, prospective applicants should not wait until November to begin preparing.

Key Takeaway for Prospective Applicants

The Winter 2027 UBC Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program presents an opportunity for eligible African applicants to pursue selected master’s degrees at the University of British Columbia.

However, prospective applicants should understand that eligibility alone does not guarantee selection. The process places importance on academic merit, transformative leadership, community service, the quality of the application, and the potential contribution of the applicant to the development of their home country.

Applicants should begin by identifying an eligible programme, confirming their academic qualifications, preparing their supporting documents, and submitting the appropriate expression of interest before the September 6, 2026 deadline.

Those invited to continue should then complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application and, if successful, proceed to the relevant UBC faculty application within the specified November deadline.

Conclusion

The UBC Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program Winter 2027 opportunity offers eligible African applicants a structured pathway toward graduate study at the University of British Columbia.

With eligible programmes spanning food and resource economics, food science, sustainable forest management, international forestry, urban forestry leadership, geomatics for environmental management, forestry research, and data science, the opportunity covers several fields connected to Africa’s development priorities and the future of sustainable communities.

Applicants who meet the eligibility requirements should begin preparing early rather than waiting for the application window to open. Academic records, CVs, reference letters, personal statements, English-language requirements, and programme eligibility should all be reviewed in advance.

The first critical deadline is September 6, 2026, for the expression of interest, followed by the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program selection stage and the November 20, 2026 final deadline for the UBC Faculty application.

Prospective applicants should carefully follow the official UBC instructions throughout every stage of the process and ensure that all required information is submitted accurately and on time.

item.content:encoded:
The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund Creative Catalyst Fellowship 2027 is now accepting applications from individual artists whose creative work engages the public on important issues affecting Asian American and Pacific Islander communities.

The yearlong fellowship provides up to eight selected artists with $30,000 each to create work inspired by the 2027 theme, “Belonging.” The programme is designed to give independent artists the financial resources, creative freedom, community connections, and communications support needed to develop ambitious work that can reach wider audiences and encourage meaningful civic participation.

The fellowship is more than a financial award for artistic production. Selected Fellows become part of a cohort that participates in peer learning, a required in-person retreat, virtual check-ins, and opportunities to connect their creative practice with broader conversations about social justice, community, inclusion, identity, and civic engagement.

The 2027 Creative Catalyst Fellowship runs from January through December 2027, with selected artwork expected to be completed by August 15, 2027.

The application deadline is Thursday, October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.

About the AAPI Civic Engagement Fund Creative Catalyst Fellowship

The Creative Catalyst Fellowship is an initiative of the AAPI Civic Engagement Fund that recognizes the power of art to influence public conversations and encourage civic participation.

The programme supports individual artists whose work addresses significant issues facing AAPI communities and has the potential to connect with audiences beyond traditional artistic spaces.

The fellowship is based on the idea that creative work can play an important role in social change.

Art can:

  • Start conversations about difficult social issues
  • Help communities express their experiences
  • Challenge stereotypes and misconceptions
  • Encourage people to think differently
  • Build connections across communities
  • Make complex social issues more accessible
  • Create opportunities for civic participation
  • Highlight experiences that may otherwise remain unheard
  • Encourage greater understanding and inclusion

Through the Creative Catalyst Fellowship, the AAPI Civic Engagement Fund seeks to provide artists with the resources and freedom to develop meaningful work while also helping that work reach broader audiences.

2027 Fellowship Theme: Belonging

The central theme for the 2027 Creative Catalyst Fellowship is “Belonging.”

Belonging can be understood as the feeling of being accepted, valued, connected, and able to participate fully in a community.

For the purposes of this fellowship, the theme encompasses ideas such as:

  • Community
  • Home
  • Identity
  • Agency
  • Inclusion
  • Safety
  • Participation
  • Cultural connection
  • Representation
  • Collective wellbeing
  • The right of communities to flourish

The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund describes belonging as a counterweight to racism and violence and connects it to a broader vision of inclusion that recognizes the contributions AAPI communities have made to the United States.

Artists are therefore encouraged to consider how their creative practice can explore the meaning of belonging and contribute to public conversations around this theme.

What Does “Belonging” Mean for Artists?

The theme is broad enough to accommodate different artistic disciplines and perspectives.

An artist could potentially explore questions such as:

  • What does it mean to feel at home?
  • How do migration and displacement influence belonging?
  • How do communities preserve cultural identity?
  • What happens when people experience exclusion?
  • How can art challenge racism and violence?
  • How do different generations understand belonging?
  • How can communities create more inclusive spaces?
  • What does civic participation look like within AAPI communities?
  • How can creative expression strengthen connections between people?
  • How have AAPI communities shaped American society?

Artists should, however, ensure that their proposed projects clearly connect with the fellowship’s published theme and broader purpose.

$30,000 Creative Catalyst Fellowship Award

One of the most significant benefits of the Creative Catalyst Fellowship is the $30,000 award provided to each selected artist.

The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund plans to select up to eight artists, meaning the programme could provide up to $240,000 in total fellowship awards if all eight fellowship places are filled.

The financial support gives independent artists an opportunity to devote resources and time to the development of substantial creative projects.

Rather than simply recognizing work that has already been completed, the fellowship is designed to help artists produce new work with the potential to reach broader audiences and stimulate public discussion.

What Do Fellows Receive?

Selected Fellows receive more than the $30,000 award.

The fellowship provides a combination of:

  • Financial support
  • Peer learning
  • Creative community
  • Professional development
  • Communications assistance
  • Publicity and promotion
  • Digital advertising
  • Community introductions
  • Exhibition opportunities
  • Potential reproduction and distribution support

These resources are intended to help Fellows move their projects from creative development to public engagement.

A Yearlong Fellowship Programme

The Creative Catalyst Fellowship is a yearlong programme running from January through December 2027.

During the fellowship period, selected artists are expected to participate in several programme activities and complete their proposed creative work.

The fellowship timeline currently includes:

  • Fellowship announcement: January 14, 2027
  • Fellows Retreat: February 16–18, 2027
  • Artwork completion deadline: August 15, 2027
  • Promotion of completed artwork: August–December 2027

The organizers note that dates are subject to change.

Required Fellowship Participation

Although the fellowship provides artists with considerable creative freedom, selected Fellows have several required responsibilities.

Fellows must:

  1. Attend a virtual orientation at the beginning of the fellowship.
  2. Attend the required two-day in-person Creative Catalyst Fellows Retreat.
  3. Participate in virtual check-ins throughout the fellowship.
  4. Complete their proposed artwork by the designated deadline.
  5. Submit a Narrative Report.

The programme therefore requires a meaningful commitment from selected artists.

Applicants should consider these obligations carefully before applying.

Creative Catalyst Fellows Retreat

One of the central components of the programme is the Creative Catalyst Fellows Retreat, scheduled for February 16–18, 2027.

Attendance is required.

The location of the 2027 retreat is still to be finalized.

The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund will cover travel and accommodation costs associated with the retreat.

The retreat is designed to provide Fellows with an opportunity to:

  • Learn about critical issues affecting AAPI communities
  • Connect with community-based organizations and initiatives
  • Meet fellow Creative Catalyst artists
  • Exchange ideas
  • Develop relationships
  • Explore connections between creative practice and social justice
  • Better understand community work on the ground

The retreat is therefore not simply a networking event. It is intended to help artists situate their creative work within broader community and social justice movements.

Peer Learning and Cohort Experience

Up to eight artists will form the 2027 Creative Catalyst cohort.

Working as part of a cohort allows Fellows to exchange perspectives with artists working in different disciplines and creative traditions.

This can be particularly valuable for independent artists, who may otherwise work largely on their own.

Through peer sharing and learning, Fellows can:

  • Receive feedback on their ideas
  • Learn from other artists
  • Develop professional relationships
  • Discover new approaches to civic engagement
  • Explore interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Strengthen their understanding of community issues

The cohort model is an important part of the fellowship because the programme seeks to connect individual creative work with collective learning.

Communications Support

The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund will provide communications support to help selected Fellows increase the visibility of their completed projects.

The programme includes access to an accomplished communications consultant who can help place local and national news stories about the Fellows’ work in connection with the AAPI Civic Engagement Fund.

This can help artists who may have strong creative work but limited experience with media outreach or public communications.

Communications support may potentially help Fellows:

  • Develop media strategies
  • Identify appropriate media opportunities
  • Position their work for broader audiences
  • Generate public interest
  • Connect artistic projects with relevant conversations

Digital Advertising

The fellowship also provides potential support through digital advertising.

Digital promotion may be used to increase awareness of completed creative projects and support the broader mission of the AAPI Civic Engagement Fund.

This is particularly important because the fellowship emphasizes the potential for projects to reach audiences beyond the artist’s immediate community.

Community Introductions

Selected artists may receive introductions to AAPI organizations that could potentially use their completed work for charitable purposes.

These connections can help artists develop relationships with community organizations and identify practical ways their work can contribute to civic or community engagement.

For example, a completed project may potentially be relevant to:

  • Community education
  • Cultural programming
  • Advocacy
  • Public discussions
  • Awareness campaigns
  • Community events
  • Social justice initiatives

The actual opportunities available will depend on the nature of the artist’s work and the relevance of potential organizational partnerships.

Exhibition Placement

The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund may also support Fellows in placing their work in:

  • Galleries
  • Exhibitions
  • Shows
  • Other appropriate venues

Priority will be given to venues experienced in presenting art connected to social justice themes.

This can provide an important pathway for artists seeking to move their work beyond its initial production stage and into broader public presentation.

Replica Development and Distribution

Another potential fellowship offering is replica development.

The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund may support the production and distribution of materials such as:

  • Posters
  • Books
  • Calendars
  • Stickers

These materials can help extend the life and reach of an artistic project.

Instead of limiting the impact of a project to a single exhibition or original artwork, reproduction can make elements of the work accessible to larger audiences and organizations.

All such support is subject to availability and relevance to the project’s needs.

Who Can Apply for the Creative Catalyst Fellowship?

The fellowship is intended for individual artists.

The programme is particularly relevant to artists whose work:

  • Engages the public
  • Addresses important issues facing AAPI communities
  • Connects with the theme of belonging
  • Has potential to reach broader audiences
  • Can encourage conversation
  • Can contribute to civic participation
  • Fits within the broader social justice objectives of the programme

The fellowship is therefore not designed as a general arts grant for any type of creative project.

The proposed work must have a meaningful connection to the programme’s purpose.

What Types of Artists May Be Suitable?

The supplied announcement does not limit the fellowship to one particular artistic discipline.

This broad approach means artists working across different creative forms may potentially be considered, provided their work satisfies the fellowship’s eligibility requirements and addresses the programme’s goals.

Potentially relevant forms of artistic practice may include:

  • Visual art
  • Illustration
  • Photography
  • Film
  • Multimedia art
  • Performance
  • Literary work
  • Design
  • Sculpture
  • Installation
  • Community-based creative practice
  • Other forms of independent artistic expression

Applicants should not assume that a particular discipline is automatically eligible. The official FAQ should be consulted for the definitive eligibility requirements.

What Makes a Strong Creative Catalyst Fellowship Project?

A strong proposal should demonstrate a clear relationship between the artist’s creative practice, the fellowship theme, AAPI communities, and civic engagement.

Applicants should consider the following elements.

1. Clear Connection to Belonging

The proposed project should have a thoughtful and meaningful relationship with the 2027 theme.

Applicants should explain what aspect of belonging their work explores and why that subject matters.

2. Public Engagement

The fellowship is designed for work that engages the public.

Applicants should therefore explain who they hope to reach and how audiences might interact with, experience, or respond to the work.

3. Connection to AAPI Communities

The project should meaningfully engage with critical issues affecting Asian American and Pacific Islander communities.

Applicants should avoid superficial references to AAPI communities and instead demonstrate a genuine connection between the proposed work and the communities or issues being addressed.

4. Civic Potential

The fellowship emphasizes civic participation.

Applicants should explain how their creative project could encourage:

  • Dialogue
  • Awareness
  • Participation
  • Community connection
  • Reflection
  • Public discussion
  • Collective action

5. Potential for Broader Reach

The Fund is interested in work that can break through to broader audiences.

Applicants should therefore consider how their project could reach people beyond their immediate artistic or professional circles.

6. Artistic Quality

The proposed work should demonstrate the artist’s creative ability and a strong artistic vision.

Applicants should use their application and portfolio materials to demonstrate the quality and originality of their practice.

Fellowship Application Process

Applications for the 2027 Creative Catalyst Fellowship opened on August 13, 2026.

Interested artists must complete the official application form before the deadline.

The application deadline is:

Thursday, October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time

Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their materials because online applications can take time to complete and technical problems can occur.

Optional Information Sessions

The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund is offering optional information sessions to introduce prospective applicants to the Creative Catalyst Fellowship and application process.

The same programme will be offered twice:

Tuesday, September 1, 2026
3:00 p.m.–4:00 p.m. Pacific Time

Friday, September 4, 2026
12:00 p.m.–1:00 p.m. Pacific Time

These sessions can be particularly useful for applicants who want to understand the programme before preparing their applications.

Although attendance is optional, prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to participate if they have questions about the fellowship or application process.

Register for the webinar here.

2027 Creative Catalyst Fellowship Timeline

The fellowship follows a structured timeline from application through production and promotion.

Date Activity
August 13, 2026 Call for submissions opens
September 1, 2026 Optional information webinar, 3:00–4:00 p.m. PT
September 4, 2026 Optional information webinar, 12:00–1:00 p.m. PT
October 15, 2026 Application deadline, 11:59 p.m. PT
January 14, 2027 Fellowship announcement
February 16–18, 2027 Required Creative Catalyst Fellows Retreat
January–December 2027 Fellowship programme
August 15, 2027 Artwork completion deadline
August–December 2027 Promotion of completed artwork

The organizers indicate that dates are subject to change.

Fellowship Requirements

Selected Fellows are required to participate in several activities during the year.

Virtual Orientation

Fellows must attend a virtual orientation at the beginning of the programme.

This orientation will help participants understand the fellowship structure, expectations, cohort experience, and programme requirements.

Creative Catalyst Retreat

Attendance at the February 2027 retreat is mandatory.

The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund will cover travel and accommodation.

Virtual Check-Ins

Fellows will participate in virtual check-ins throughout the fellowship.

These check-ins provide opportunities to maintain communication with the cohort and fellowship organizers.

Narrative Report

Each Fellow must submit a Narrative Report.

The report provides an opportunity to document the progress and outcomes of the fellowship-supported creative work.

Completion of Artwork

The selected project must be completed by August 15, 2027, according to the current programme timeline.

Applicants should therefore propose a project that is ambitious but realistically achievable within the fellowship period.

Are Additional AAPI Fund Events Mandatory?

Fellows may be invited to participate in AAPI Civic Engagement Fund events and may be asked to showcase their artwork.

However, the announcement specifies that attendance at these additional events is optional.

This distinguishes them from the required orientation, retreat, virtual check-ins, and reporting requirements.

Previous Creative Catalyst Fellows

The Creative Catalyst Fellowship has previously supported artists developing work connected to social issues affecting AAPI communities.

The AAPI Civic Engagement Fund highlights previous projects such as:

“Silis” by 2025–2026 Fellow Sargylana Cherepanova

and

“Anxieties of an Immigrant Father” by 2023–2024 Fellow Safwat Saleem.

These examples demonstrate the range of creative approaches that can be supported through the fellowship.

Applicants can review the work of previous Fellows to better understand the type of creative and socially engaged work that has been supported.

However, applicants should not attempt to copy previous projects. Instead, they should focus on developing an original proposal that reflects their own creative practice and responds meaningfully to the 2027 theme of belonging.

Can Previous Creative Catalyst Fellows Apply Again?

Yes, but there is a waiting period.

Previously awarded Creative Catalyst Fellows can reapply three years after completing their previous fellowship.

Artists who have previously received the fellowship should therefore calculate their eligibility based on the date they completed their previous fellowship.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Artists can improve their applications by approaching the process strategically.

Research the Fellowship Thoroughly

Before writing the proposal, applicants should understand:

  • The purpose of the Creative Catalyst Fellowship
  • The 2027 theme of belonging
  • The programme’s focus on AAPI communities
  • The emphasis on civic engagement
  • The expected fellowship commitments
  • The available communications and promotional support

Develop a Specific Project

Avoid submitting an overly broad description of an artistic career.

The application should focus on a specific project that can be developed during the fellowship period.

Explain the Social Relevance

Applicants should explain why the issue matters and how the project responds to real experiences, challenges, or opportunities affecting AAPI communities.

Describe the Audience

Clearly identify the audiences the project is intended to reach.

Consider:

  • Who will see the work?
  • Where will they encounter it?
  • How will they interact with it?
  • What conversation should it generate?
  • How might it encourage civic participation?

Demonstrate Feasibility

The project must be completed within the fellowship timeline.

Applicants should therefore develop a realistic production schedule.

Use a Strong Portfolio

Where portfolio materials are requested, applicants should select work that best demonstrates:

  • Artistic quality
  • Originality
  • Technical ability
  • Creative voice
  • Social engagement
  • Ability to complete substantial projects

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the 2027 Creative Catalyst Fellowship is:

Thursday, October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.

Applicants should pay close attention to the Pacific Time deadline, particularly if applying from another U.S. time zone or from outside the United States.

How to Apply

Interested artists should complete the official Creative Catalyst Fellowship Application Form provided by the AAPI Civic Engagement Fund.

Before submitting, applicants should:

  1. Review the official eligibility requirements and FAQ.
  2. Understand the 2027 theme, “Belonging.”
  3. Develop a clear creative project proposal.
  4. Explain the project’s connection to AAPI communities.
  5. Demonstrate its potential for public engagement and civic participation.
  6. Prepare the required application materials.
